title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 23-27). Grothendieck works axiomatically with an additive or abelian category C, linear over a ring k. From the gcd on the previous page, k is presumably Z or a PID, at least an integral domain. C contains objects Psi^i (i >= 0) with End(Psi^i) = k and Hom(Psi^i, Psi^j) = 0 for i != j. For each i there is a basic non-split extension L^i = L(i,1):
0 -> Psi^{i-1} -> L^i -> Psi^i -> 0, with class e_i.
For n >= 1 there are extensions L(i,n), the pushout of L^i along n.id on Psi^{i-1}, with class n.e_i.

Concrete model. The axioms fit exactly the category of complexes of free k-modules:
- Psi^i = k placed in degree i;
- L(i,n) = [k --n--> k] in degrees i, i-1 (homological indexing), whose subcomplex is Psi^{i-1}.
The aim is a dévissage: axiom (d) on the next page says every object is a finite extension of L(i,n)'s and Psi^j's. This is Smith normal form for complexes. It serves the study of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes and their multiplicative structures.

Previous page. It computed Hom(L(i,n), L(j,m)):
- 0 unless j = i or j = i+1;
- for j = i+1, a rank-one k-module generated by L(i,n) -> Psi^i -> L(i+1,m);
- for j = i, a rank-one k-module generated by the pair (n', m'), with n' = n/(n,m), m' = m/(n,m).
In the chain-complex model these are maps (a,b) with b.n = m.a.

This page computes Hom(L(i,n), Psi^j).

(1) Psi^j is a subobject of L^{j+1} = L(j+1,1). So Hom(L(i,n), Psi^j) embeds in Hom(L(i,n), L(j+1,1)). By the previous result this vanishes unless j+1 is i or i+1, i.e. unless j is i-1 or i.

(2) Restricting along Psi^{i-1} -> L(i,n) lands in Hom(Psi^{i-1}, Psi^j), which is 0 for j != i-1.

(3) Case j = i. Every map kills Psi^{i-1}, so it factors through the quotient Psi^i. Hence Hom = End(Psi^i) = k, with basis the canonical projection.

(4) Case j = i-1. Take alpha: L(i,n) -> Psi^{i-1} and set c = alpha.xi in End(Psi^{i-1}) = k, where xi is the inclusion. Precompose with the pushout map L^i -> L(i,n), which restricts to u.id (u = n) on Psi^{i-1}. The composite L^i -> Psi^{i-1} lies in Hom(L^i, Psi^{i-1}) = 0, since a nonzero map would give a splitting of the non-split L^i. Hence u.c = 0 in k. Since u != 0 and k has no zero divisors, c = 0. So alpha factors through Psi^i -> Psi^{i-1}, which is 0, and alpha = 0.

Conclusion: Hom(L(i,n), Psi^j) = k (basis the canonical projection L(i,n) -> Psi^i) if j = i, and 0 otherwise. In the chain model: a chain map from [k --n--> k] to k[i-1] must satisfy f.n = 0, so f = 0. The next page computes the dual Hom(Psi^i, L(j,n)).
errors: Step (4) silently uses that multiplication by u = n is injective on End(Psi^{i-1}) = k. This holds for k = Z or any torsion-free domain with n >= 1, but fails, e.g., for k a field of characteristic p with p | n. There L(i,n) splits and Hom(L(i,n), Psi^{i-1}) = k != 0. The hypothesis n >= 1 over a torsion-free k is only made explicit in axiom (d) on the next page.
The vanishing Hom(L^i, Psi^{i-1}) = 0 is used without comment. It requires the basic extension L^i to be non-split and End(Psi^{i-1}) = k to have no zero divisors.

ideas.what: Axiomatic description of a k-linear category generated by 'simple' objects Psi^i with End = k and elementary two-step extensions L(i,n) of class n.e_i, with full computation of the Hom groups between generators.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary complexes [k --n--> k] and Smith normal form / structure theorem for complexes of free modules over a PID; Hom computations in a graded quiver-like category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical homological algebra (Smith normal form; decomposition of free complexes over a PID, e.g. in Cartan-Eilenberg era texts)

ideas.what: Lemma: Hom(L(i,n), Psi^j) = k.(canonical projection) if j = i, else 0. Proved by embedding Psi^j into L^{j+1} and comparing with the pushout L^i -> L(i,n).
ideas.modern_name: Hom computation for indecomposable two-term complexes

deep.surprise_reason: A routine Hom computation in an axiomatic model of complexes of free modules over a PID. It is a step toward an abstract dévissage, correct under the implicit torsion-free hypothesis, and nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 'On connaît αξ aussi L^i = L(i,-)/Ψ^i' is garbled. The intended statement concerns the composite L^i -> L(i,-) -> Psi^{i-1}, where L^i -> L(i,-) is the pushout map inducing u.id on Psi^{i-1}; the composite lies in Hom(L^i, Psi^{i-1}) = 0.

In 'Si donc j = i, Hom(L(i,-),Ψ^i) ↪ Hom(L^i,Ψ^i) ≃ k', the target is logically Hom(Psi^i, Psi^i) ≃ k, via factorization through the quotient. The written symbol may be Psi^i or L^i; the image is ambiguous.
Top line: L^{j+1} denotes L(j+1, 1), written underneath as L(j+1,-).
